properties.draft_rule: On the river: the Bavispe's channel (the highest-order INEGI stream in the area, its main stem) and 1.5 km either side. She crosses the river, so the crossing is on it; where along this reach is still open, so the whole reach in the area stays.

The ground between the two draws: the strip between lines through the GNIS points of Clanton Draw and Foster Draw that run down the general slope of the area (the way the draws run), with 400 m beyond each. NHD does not name the draws' channels here.
Kept the whole area. The trap was off the creek road, across a pasture, about two hours' ride from Cloverdale; the area already covers the road's upper reach and the pastures either side.
Kept the whole area: the same trap site as the wolf's last stop (J1, stop 13).
On the creek road he leads the wolf down (1-08): within 500 m of the Cloverdale Creek road (Census TIGER 2023, Cloverdale Rd C001, Co Rd C001 and Co Rd C106). The area says where along the road.
The plain: ground with a slope under 3 degrees (smoothed 30 m DEM) north of the boundary at 31°20′ N, the part joined to the stop. The ranch is on the broad volcanic plain before the boundary.
Within 3 km of the boundary along 31°20′ N, where the monuments stand: they are at the line with a monument in sight.
The Bavispe's valley floor: ground within 4 km of the river and no more than 60 m above it. They ride down the river path, across a meadow to a road and south along it to the settlement (1-09).

Flat ground beside the Batepito: within 2 km of the river (INEGI streams along Natural Earth's Río Batepito), no more than 30 m above it, with a slope under 5 degrees. The book has the road on the other bank, but not which bank that is.
A promontory over the north-running Bavispe on the sierra's side: ground west of the river (its main stem in INEGI), at least 150 m above it and within 8 km of it.
The high country: ground above 1,500 m west of the upper Bavispe (west of the line Bacerac to Bavispe, extended). The book names no range, so this only drops the valleys.

The escarpment's edge: ground that looks down at least 300 m within 6 km to the east, on the west side of the upper Bavispe (its main stem in INEGI) and within 8 km of it. He looks east over the barranca and then goes down to the river.

The river town: ground within 1.5 km of the upper Bavispe (the area's main stem in INEGI) and no more than 150 m above it, so benches above the canyon floor stay. The town is across a ford on the river; which bank is not known.
On the road over the range: within 1.5 km of the Douglas to Cloverdale roads (Geronimo Trail and Cloverdale Road in Census TIGER).

The ranch house is on the road: within 2.5 km of the road north from Cloverdale (today's State Highway 338 and Cloverdale Road, Census TIGER). The book gives nine miles by road from the Parham house, so the area still fixes where along the road.
The east side of Lordsburg: the town's streets (within 250 m of Census TIGER local streets) east of the town's centre point. Today's town is larger than the town of the 1940s.
The east side of Lordsburg: the town's streets (within 250 m of Census TIGER local streets) east of the town's centre point. Today's town is larger than the town of the 1940s.
The alkali flats: the flat ground (slope under 1.5 degrees) joined to the stop, which drops the hills in the south-west. The DEM cannot tell alkali from grass, so the whole flat stays.
At the river: within 1 km of the San Simon River (NHD flowline). Where along the river is the area's estimate.
At the highway crossing, east of Bowie: within 1 km of the highway (Census TIGER primary and secondary roads) and east of the town's centre point.
On the old road south into the Dos Cabezas: within 1 km of Apache Pass Road (Census TIGER), where they camped. The book does not say how far along.
The eastern rim: ground that looks down at least 300 m within 10 km to the east, within 8 km of the line from Bacerac to Colonia Juárez.

Kept the whole area. The book has prairie below the rim; the DEM finds no plain in the area, only small flats along the streams, so the area may sit too far west of the open ground towards Colonia Juárez.
East of the road: east of the straight line from Casas Grandes to the Hacienda de San Diego (no map of the old road is to hand) and within 3 km of it, where a fire can be seen from the road.
A roadside field on the Madera road: within 2 km of the line from Las Varas to Madera (the road is not mapped here) on ground flatter than 4 degrees.
By a river near the road: within 1 km of INEGI streams of order 4 and up, and within 4 km of the line from Las Varas to Madera. The book names neither the river nor the road.
On the wagon road: within 8 km of the line La Norteña, La Babícora, Namiquipa, the road's ends and middle as the book gives them. The book's compass does not close here, so the band is wide.
On the road east to La Boquilla: within 3 km of the line from Las Varas to La Boquilla.
On the road, with the lake to the south: within 2.5 km of the line from Las Varas to La Boquilla, north of the lake and not in it.
On the road west of La Boquilla, east of the lake: within 2.5 km of the line from Las Varas to La Boquilla, west of the town and out of the lake.
Kept the whole area. They follow the tracks north from the road all afternoon and camp in a swale; the area already lies north of the road and the lake, and a swale cannot be told from the DEM.
Kept the whole area. The book gives an east-west road, a crossroads and a track down from the mountains, but no distance or landmark to cut by.
Between the road north of La Boquilla and the river to its west: west of La Boquilla and north of the lake. They leave the road a mile above the town and ride west to a river (3-08).

Kept the whole area. The camp is on a rise a mile west of the river after a night's ride (3-08), but which of the area's streams is that river is not known: cutting to the side of the largest one (in the area's north-east corner) left a sliver, which the night's ride does not support.
By the river: within 800 m of the stream nearest San José (INEGI, order 4 and up). The camp is in a cottonwood grove by the river and Boyd is shot from the far bank.
Kept the whole area. The truck meets them on a dirt road in open country; no road of the period is mapped here and most of the area is open country, so nothing narrows it.
Kept the whole area. An arroyo, a light to the north, a fence and a clay track: nothing to cut by.
Near the river breaks: within 4 km of the main river (INEGI streams of order 7). He meets the main road north at a crossroads and sleeps in a field near the river breaks.
Within earshot of the crossing: within 15 km of Las Varas, a generous reach for a train whistle at night.
Beside a stream: within 1 km of INEGI streams of order 3 and up (the Santa María headwaters on this valley floor).
The lake's edge: from 500 m inside INEGI's outline of the Babícora lake to 2 km outside it. The shore moves with the water level.
On the river: within 600 m of the main river by Mata Ortiz (the INEGI stream nearest the stop, order 5 and up). A gravel bar by the river; 'below Mata Ortiz' could also mean downstream (north).
Kept the whole area. Which Álamo is meant is unresolved; the area covers both candidates.
Kept the whole area. The truck meets them on a dirt road in open country; no road of the period is mapped here and most of the area is open country, so nothing narrows it.
The lake bed and its flats: ground within 8 m of the lowest ground in the area (Playas Lake's floor). He rides south along the flats and camps by a fence.
In the mountains on a road: ground above 1,450 m within 2 km of Census TIGER roads. The old Playas road crosses the range with snow in the pass; which road is not known.

The ranch house is on the road: within 2.5 km of the road north from Cloverdale (today's State Highway 338 and Cloverdale Road, Census TIGER). The book gives nine miles by road from the Parham house, so the area still fixes where along the road.
The open plain: the Animas Valley floor below 1,650 m with a slope under 2 degrees, the part joined to the stop.

The ranch house is on the road: within 2.5 km of the road north from Cloverdale (today's State Highway 338 and Cloverdale Road, Census TIGER). The book gives nine miles by road from the Parham house, so the area still fixes where along the road.
On the plain by the road: ground flatter than 2 degrees within 4 km of the line from Las Varas to La Boquilla, out of the lake.
The plains around the lake: ground below 2,250 m with a slope under 4 degrees (the Babícora basin floor and its swales), lake included.
On the plain: ground with a slope under 3 degrees. The cabin is a lone house on the plain on a road towards a gap in the mountains.
Kept the whole area. It is already small (3 km²); a bench in low hills is below what the 30 m DEM can find reliably.
Where the town's lights show: ground in sight of a light 10 m up at Nuevo Casas Grandes (viewshed of the 30 m DEM, eye at 2 m) and east of the town.
At the river: within 1 km of the Casas Grandes River (the INEGI stream nearest Corralitos, order 6). He reaches the river and follows a trail north beside it.
On the river trail: within 1 km of the Casas Grandes River (INEGI, order 6).
At the boundary: within 1.5 km of the line along 31°47′ N. He passes an obelisk on the line; where along it is the area's estimate.
South of the town: the part of the area south of Animas's centre point.
On the road over the pass: within 1 km of NM 152 (Census TIGER), the old road east over Emory Pass.
By the blacktop: within 500 m of the highways in the area (Census TIGER secondary roads, NM 152 and NM 27). The waystation's adobes stand by the highway.
